newDescription:
In this Year 6 English lesson, pupils learn how to choose between formal and informal writing by considering purpose and audience, and how the subjunctive can strengthen formal writing.

This lesson includes:
✔ Distinguishing formal and informal writing across texts such as messages, emails, letters, essays, diaries, reports, stories and information texts
✔ Understanding how audience and purpose affect the level of formality
✔ Identifying features of formal writing, including a serious tone, precise vocabulary, correct grammar and punctuation, and more complex sentence structures
✔ Identifying features of informal writing, including conversational language, contractions, abbreviations, text-message language and clichés
✔ Using the subjunctive form to express imagined situations, wishes, advice, requests, demands and suggestions
✔ Using were for imagined situations, for example if I were you
✔ Using the basic verb form after formal reporting verbs such as suggest, propose, require and demand
✔ Using the subjunctive after formal expressions such as it is desirable, necessary, vital and essential
✔ Analysing the structure, vocabulary and tone of a formal complaint letter
✔ Identifying formal linking phrases and subject-specific vocabulary in context
✔ Applying formal-letter conventions when writing a response

Pupils begin by comparing different forms of writing and deciding whether they are usually formal, informal or capable of being both. They then examine the language features that create a formal or informal tone.

The lesson moves on to the subjunctive, beginning with familiar advice such as if I were you before developing more formal patterns. Pupils see how the verb form can remain unchanged after subjects in constructions involving requests, proposals, demands and suggestions.

A detailed formal complaint letter is then analysed for layout, tone, vocabulary, cohesion and subjunctive constructions. Pupils use this model to support their own formal response.

By the end of the lesson, learners will be able to adapt their writing to audience and purpose, recognise the key differences between formal and informal style, and use common subjunctive forms appropriately in formal writing.
